documents.title: Neurology follow-up (visit 01/27/2026)
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROMUSCULAR CLINIC: FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 01/27/2026

Diagnoses: myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DMPK ~420 CTG repeats); Klinefelter syndrome 47,XXY; first-degree AV block with intermittent second-degree type I block (cardiology following); bilateral cataract extraction at 20.

Interval history: Handshakes are again hard to release. He notices his face is weaker, food is harder to get down, and he has lost weight without trying. He also reports less interest in sex than before.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol. Works part-time in retail.

Examination: Wasting of the temporalis and masseter muscles on both sides. Atrophy of the intrinsic muscles of the hands. Grip myotonia persists. Heart rhythm irregular on auscultation.

Laboratory (drawn today): CK 120 U/L (ref 38-174). Fasting glucose 90 mg/dL. Total testosterone 220 ng/dL, low. FSH 15 mIU/mL and LH 14 mIU/mL, both elevated.
ECG today: first-degree heart block.

Impression: Progression of DM1 with bulbar involvement (dysphagia) and weight loss. Primary testicular failure, as expected with Klinefelter syndrome, now with low testosterone and reduced libido.

Plan:
1. Modified barium swallow with speech-language pathology.
2. Continue yearly cardiology surveillance; irregular rhythm noted today.
3. Low testosterone to be addressed by primary care.
4. Return to clinic in 12 months.

cc: primary care

documents.title: Modified barium swallow study (02/24/2026)
documents.author: speech-language pathology
documents.body:
MODIFIED BARIUM SWALLOW STUDY
Date: 02/24/2026
Referred by: neuromuscular clinic, DM1 with dysphagia

Consistencies: thin and nectar-thick liquid by cup and straw, puree, soft solid, cracker.

Findings: Oral phase with mildly reduced bolus control. Swallow initiation delayed. Pharyngeal residue in the valleculae and pyriform sinuses after solids, cleared with a second swallow. No laryngeal penetration or aspiration with any consistency.

Impression: Mild oropharyngeal dysphagia.

Recommendations: Regular diet. Small bites, eat slowly, alternate solids with sips of liquid, use a second swallow as needed. Repeat study if symptoms progress.

Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: Follow-up after neurology: swallowing, weight loss, low testosterone

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here after his January neuromuscular visit and the swallow study. Food, meat and bread especially, feels like it hangs up and he has to swallow twice. No choking, no coughing with drinks, no pneumonia. Face feels weaker and friends say he looks thinner in the face. Has lost weight without trying. Eating three meals but slower. Sex drive lower than a year or two ago. Mood ok, PHQ-9 4.

O: Wt 72.5 (75 in Nov, 77.5 last Jan). BP/HR fine. Temporal and masseter hollowing. Thenar and interosseous wasting both hands, slow grip release. Heart irregular at times, no murmur. Lungs clear.

Swallow study 2/24: mild oropharyngeal dysphagia, residue clears with second swallow, no aspiration. Regular diet with strategies.

A/P
1. Oropharyngeal dysphagia, DM1. Follow SLP strategies; he has the handout. Call for choking, cough with meals or fevers.
2. Unintentional weight loss, about 5 kg in a year. Likely DM1 progression with slower eating. Calorie-dense snacks between meals. CBC, CMP, TSH, A1c today. Weigh at each visit.
3. Low testosterone (220 at neurology, high FSH/LH) with lower libido. Repeat morning testosterone drawn now, 08:30. Will discuss treatment and fertility at next visit.
4. DM1, conduction disease, Klinefelter: per specialists.
RTC 4 weeks.

documents.title: Testosterone and other labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Zachary, your morning testosterone came back at 228, low again and close to the neurology result. Blood count, chemistry, thyroid and A1c are normal. Before we talk about testosterone treatment we need to talk about whether you and your partner still want to try for a biological child, because testosterone can make that harder. We'll go over it on April 1.

documents.body: Yeah we still want to try at some point. We'll talk about it before the appointment. Thanks.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Follow-up. Swallowing about the same, using the second swallow and sips, no choking. Eating more snacks. Libido still low, no other complaints. He and his partner talked it over: they still hope to have a biological child at some point and want to know their options before he starts anything.

O: Wt 72.0 (72.5 in March). BP/HR normal. Facial and hand wasting as before. Heart irregular at times.

Labs: AM testosterone 228 (3/3), 220 with FSH 15 and LH 14 at neurology (1/27). CBC, CMP, TSH, A1c normal.

A/P
1. Male hypogonadism, primary (testicular), Klinefelter. Two low morning values with high gonadotropins. Testosterone would help libido, energy and bone, but it shuts down what little sperm production there may be. Agreed to see reproductive urology first about sperm retrieval options; no testosterone for now. Referral placed.
2. Weight loss, slowing. Continue extra calories. Recheck weight next visit.
3. Dysphagia: SLP strategies.
4. DM1 with conduction disease: cardiology yearly visit coming up in May.
Physical in the fall.
